newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures slump, June bonds end down sharply.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures slump, June bonds end down sharply.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended sharply lower, never recovering from technical weakness and March jobs data earlier.
Traders zeroed in on the 0.4-percent gain in average hourly earnings in the March non-farm payrolls report, saying the wage gain is evidence for more Fed rate hikes down the road.

March U.S. jobs rose 175,000 compared with a revised 293,000 in February and a forecast for 196,000. The jobless rate edged down to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent, in line with expectations. The average workweek fell to 34.8 hours from 34.9 hours and average hourly earnings gained to $12.15 from $12.10.

June T-bonds slid through support at 107-00 and through Tuesday's low of 106-25/32 to hit a session low of 106-23/32. Traders noted that support at the seven-month low of 106-22/32 held, but many said September 1996 lows in the lower 105-00 handle are intermediate term targets.
"Nothing has changed here whatsoever," said Michael Boss, floor analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston. "The market couldn't muster any kind of rally and we traded through a new seven-month low," he said.
He said the downward sloping trading channels continue in five-year and ten-year notes and in bonds.
One T-bonds options trader said the market continues to be vulnerable to any type of strong news.
"You're still in a situation where any time you get strong data they think the Fed's going to raise rates again," the trader said.
He noted a "sell-the-bounce" mentality whenever outright selling pressure ebbed.
"It's kind of a slow grind down," he said, noting that a "tame" Dow Jones Industrial Average may have underpinned the sagging bond market.

At the close, June T-bonds were down 20/32 at 107-00, notes fell 10/32 to 105-17/32, munis lost 18/32 to 111-23/32, Sep bills lost 0.025 bps to 94.275, Sept Euros fell 0.030 to 93.695. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
